arxiv-2012-01579.creator: V. Angeles, F.A. Godínez, J.A. Puente-Velazquez, R. Mendez, E. Lauga, R. Zenit
arxiv-2012-01579.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by V. Angeles, F.A. Godínez, J.A. Puente-Velazquez, R. Mendez, E. Lauga, R. Zenit. We conduct experiments with force-free magnetically-driven rigid helical swimmers in Newtonian and viscoelastic (Boger) fluids. arxiv-2012-06453.title: Better call Surrogates: A hybrid Evolutionary Algorithm for Hyperparameter optimization
arxiv-2012-06453.creator: Subhodip Biswas, Adam D. Cobb, Andreea Sistrunk, Naren Ramakrishnan, Brian Jalaian
arxiv-2012-06453.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a surrogate-assisted evolutionary algorithm (EA) for hyperparameter optimization of machine learning (ML) models. The proposed SteaDE model initially estimates the objective function landscape using Radial Basis Function interpolation, and then transfers the knowledge to an EA technique called Differential Evolution that is used to evolve new solutions guided by a Bayesian optimization framework.

arxiv-2104-09175.title: BrFAST: a Tool to Select Browser Fingerprinting Attributes for Web Authentication According to a Usability-Security Trade-off
arxiv-2104-09175.creator: Nampoina Andriamilanto, Tristan Allard
arxiv-2104-09175.description: Abstract . In this demonstration, we put ourselves in the place of a website manager who seeks to use browser fingerprinting for web authentication. The first step is to choose the attributes to implement among the hundreds that are available.

arxiv-2201-05249.title: An Empirical Study of Least Squares Ratings for USA Ultimate Frisbee
arxiv-2201-05249.creator: Alexander N. Sietsema
arxiv-2201-05249.description: Abstract Ultimate frisbee is one of the fastest-growing sports in the world. In the United States, the governing body USA Ultimate uses a custom power rating system to determine bid allocations for various competitive tournaments. However, this rating system has significant flaws and leaves room for improvement.

arxiv-2204-01213.title: Learning Linear Symmetries in Data Using Moment Matching
arxiv-2204-01213.creator: Colin Hagemeyer
arxiv-2204-01213.description: Abstract It is common in machine learning and statistics to use symmetries derived from expert knowledge to simplify problems or improve performance, using methods like data augmentation or penalties. In this paper we consider the unsupervised and semi-supervised problems of learning such symmetries in a distribution directly from data in a model-free fashion.

arxiv-2310-02441.title: Finding the dispersing siblings of young open clusters
arxiv-2310-02441.creator: E. Vaher, D. Hobbs, P. McMillan, T. Prusti
arxiv-2310-02441.description: Abstract Context. Stars tend to form in clusters, but many escape their birth clusters very early. Identifying the escaped members of clusters can inform us about the dissolution of star clusters, but also about the stellar dynamics in the galaxy.

arxiv-2312-05684.title: Light detection and Cosmic Rejection in the ICARUS LArTPC at Fermilab
arxiv-2312-05684.creator: A. Heggestuen
arxiv-2312-05684.description: Abstract The ICARUS-T600 detector is a 760-ton Liquid Argon Time Projection Chamber (LArTPC) currently operating at Fermilab as the Far Detector in the Short Baseline Neutrino (SBN) program. The SBN program is composed of three LArTPCs with a central goal of testing the sterile neutrino hypothesis.

arxiv-2412-10713.title: RAT: Adversarial Attacks on Deep Reinforcement Agents for Targeted Behaviors
arxiv-2412-10713.creator: Fengshuo Bai, Runze Liu, Yali Du, Ying Wen, Yaodong Yang
arxiv-2412-10713.description: Abstract Evaluating deep reinforcement learning (DRL) agents against targeted behavior attacks is critical for assessing their robustness. These attacks aim to manipulate the victim into specific behaviors that align with the attacker’s objectives, often bypassing traditional reward-based defenses. Prior methods have primarily focused on reducing cumulative rewards; however, rewards are typically too generic to capture complex safety requirements effectively.

arxiv-2412-15439.title: Uncertainty Estimation for Super-Resolution using ESRGAN
arxiv-2412-15439.creator: Maniraj Sai Adapa 1 , Marco Zullich 1 and Matias Valdenegro-Toro 1 1 Department of AI, University of Groningen, Nijenborgh 9, 9747AG, Groningen, Netherlands manirajadapa@gmail.com, m.zullich, m.a.valdenegro.toro@rug.nl
arxiv-2412-15439.description: Abstract Deep Learning–based image super-resolution (SR) has been gaining traction with the ad of Generative Adversarial Networks. Models like SRGAN and ESRGAN are constantly ranked between the best image SR tools. However, they lack principled ways for estimating predictive uncertainty. In the present work, we enhance these models using Monte Carlo–Dropout and Deep Ensemble, allowing the computation of predictive uncertainty.

arxiv-2501-06445.title: Self-dual pp-wave solutions in chiral higher-spin gravity
arxiv-2501-06445.creator: Tung Tran
arxiv-2501-06445.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tung Tran. We show that chiral higher-spin gravity with a vanishing cosmological constant admits a class of exact self-dual pp-wave solutions derived from harmonic scalar functions and two principal spinors. These solutions satisfy both the linear and non-linear equations of motion, as they annihilate all higher-order vertices, leading to the equations of motion for free fields on a self-dual background sourced by a positive-helicity spin-2 field. Our method employs a simple Kerr-Schild ansatz for positive-helicity chiral higher-spin fields adapted to the self-dual gravity framework.

arxiv-2505-17083.title: Scale-invariant attention
arxiv-2505-17083.creator: Ben Anson, Xi Wang, Laurence Aitchison
arxiv-2505-17083.description: Abstract One persistent challenge in LLM research is the development of attention mechanisms that are able to generalise from training on shorter contexts to inference on longer contexts. We propose two conditions that we expect all effective long-context attention mechanisms to have: scale-invariant total attention, and scale-invariant attention sparsity.

arxiv-2505-18086.title: Stable Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Reasoning
arxiv-2505-18086.creator: Muzhi Dai, Shixuan Liu, Qingyi Si
arxiv-2505-18086.description: Abstract The success of Deepseek-R1 has drawn the LLM community’s attention to reinforcement learning (RL) methods like GRPO. However, such rule-based 0/1 outcome reward methods lack the capability to regulate the intermediate reasoning processes during chain-of-thought (CoT) generation, leading to severe overthinking phenomena.

arxiv-2601-17329.title: Conformal Feedback Alignment: Quantifying Answer-Level Reliability for Robust LLM Alignment
arxiv-2601-17329.creator: Tiejin Chen, Xiaoou Liu, Vishnu Nandam, Kuan-Ru Liou, Hua Wei
arxiv-2601-17329.description: Abstract Preference-based alignment like Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) learns from pairwise preferences, yet the labels are often noisy and inconsistent. Existing uncertainty-aware approaches weight preferences, but ignore a more fundamental factor: the reliability of the answers being compared.

pmc-10614413.title: Intestinal helminth co-infection and associated factors among pulmonary tuberculosis patients in Africa and Asia: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-10614413.creator: Yohannes Zenebe, Meseret Habtamu, Markos Abebe, Begna Tulu, Abay Atnafu, Daniel Mekonnen, Roland Lang, Abaineh Munshea
pmc-10614413.description: IntroductionTuberculosis (TB) and intestinal helminths have huge public health importance, and they are geographically overlapped. Data about the burden of intestinal helminth and TB co-infection in these areas are fragmented. In this systematic review and meta-analysis we compile the current literatures and generate pooled prevalence. We also identity factors associated with intestinal helminth co-infection among TB patients.

pmc-11335111.creator: Xinglin Liu, Yu Chen, Yan Xiong, Yanlin Wu, Hai Long, Hai Long, Hai Long, Hai Long
pmc-11335111.description: Although the impact of interest rates, repayment periods, and loan scales on loan consequences has been extensively studied, little attention has been paid to the geographical distance involved in loan transactions. This study collects the addresses of borrowing companies, listed companies, and banks.

pmc-11369396.title: Metabolic profiling and spatial metabolite distribution in wild soybean (G. soja) and cultivated soybean (G. max) seeds
pmc-11369396.creator: Xin Yin, Zhentao Ren, Ruizong Jia, Xiaodong Wang, Qi Yu, Li Zhang, Laipan Liu, Wenjing Shen, Zhixiang Fang, Jingang Liang, Biao Liu
pmc-11369396.description: Wild soybeans retain many substances significantly reduced or lost in cultivars during domestication. This study utilized LC-MS to analyze metabolites in the seed coats and embryos of wild and cultivated soybeans. 866 and 815 metabolites were identified in the seed extracts of both soybean types, with 35 and 10 significantly differing metabolites in the seed coat and embryos, respectively.

pmc-11378149.title: Fluorinated Nanosized Zeolitic-Imidazolate Frameworks as Potential Devices for Mechanical Energy Storage
pmc-11378149.creator: Eder Amayuelas, Judit Farrando-Perez, Alexander Missyul, Yaroslav Grosu, Joaquin Silvestre-Albero, Carolina Carrillo-Carrión
pmc-11378149.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Fluorination is one of the most efficient and universal strategies to increase the hydrophobicity of materials and consequently their water stability. Zeolitic-imidazolate frameworks (ZIFs), which have limited stability in aqueous media and even lower stability when synthesized on a nanometric scale, can greatly benefit from the incorporation of fluorine atoms, not only to improve their stability but also to provide additional properties.

pmc-11451839.title: Appendiceal Bleeding, A Rare Yet Important Cause of Lower Gastrointestinal Bleed
pmc-11451839.creator: Ayman Tabcheh, Johny Salem, Karim Zodeh, Ammar Ghazale
pmc-11451839.description: BackgroundLower gastrointestinal bleeding accounts for 20 to 25% of all gastrointestinal bleedings. Appendiceal bleeding is a rare, yet important cause of lower gastrointestinal bleed; in many cases, it can be misdiagnosed as obscure gastrointestinal bleeding. Here, we present a case of appendiceal bleeding in an elderly female.Case descriptionA 79-year-old female presented with acute onset of gastrointestinal bleeding of same-day duration.

pmc-11608350.title: Validation studies of the FLASH-TV system to passively measure children’s TV viewing
pmc-11608350.creator: Anil Kumar Vadathya, Tatyana Garza, Uzair Alam, Alex Ho, Salma MA Musaad, Alicia Beltran, Jennette P Moreno, Tom Baranowski, Nimah Haidar, Sheryl O Hughes, Jason A Mendoza, Ashok Veeraraghavan, Joseph Young, Akane Sano, Teresia M O’Connor
pmc-11608350.description: TV viewing is associated with health risks, but existing measures of TV viewing are imprecise due to relying on self-report. We developed the Family Level Assessment of Screen use in the Home (FLASH)-TV, a machine learning pipeline with state-of-the-art computer vision methods to measure children’s TV viewing.

pmc-12700303.title: Bilateral Upper and Lower Limb Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS) in a Lung Cancer Survivor: Diagnostic and Interventional Challenges in the Setting of Radiculopathy and Prior Radiotherapy
pmc-12700303.creator: Tim Hsu, Shivang Patel, Jake Belli, Zachary Siegel, Kamal T Patel
pmc-12700303.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). We present the case of a 64-year-old man with an unusual and diagnostically challenging presentation of Complex Regional Pain Syndrome (CRPS) Type I involving both the left upper and lower extremities. His illness was precipitated by an on-the-job injury and was further complicated by a prior history of adenocarcinoma of the lung treated with radiation, resulting in severe left upper extremity (LUE) weakness along with cervical and lumbar radiculopathy.

pmc-13227218.title: A renally clearable tumor-targeted probe enabling functional delineation of tumor margins by NIR-II fluorescence lifetime imaging
pmc-13227218.creator: Jin Zhang, Jiuling Liao, Dong Han, Xingsheng Ren, Dehong Hu, Duyang Gao, Pengfei Zhang, Shengnan Yuan, Wei Zheng, Christopher J. Butch, Bo Dai, Huiming Cai, Yiqing Wang, Hairong Zheng, Zonghai Sheng
pmc-13227218.description: Accurate intraoperative delineation of tumor margins remains a major clinical challenge because conventional fluorescence imaging is strongly influenced by probe concentration, tissue heterogeneity, and imaging conditions. Here, we report a renally clearable, tumor-targeted molecular probe, NY-07, for quantitative tumor-margin delineation using second near-infrared (NIR-II) fluorescence lifetime (FLT) imaging.

pmc-13531120.title: Dihydrotestosterone Induces Keratinocyte Apoptosis by Activating ERK Signaling
pmc-13531120.creator: JUNG-IL KANG, YOUN KYUNG CHOI, SANG-CHUL HAN, CHANG-GU HYUN, HYE-JIN BOO, JIN WON HYUN, EUN-SOOK YOO, HEE-KYOUNG KANG
pmc-13531120.description: Background/AimDihydrotestosterone (DHT) plays a critical role in hair loss. However, research on DHT has mostly focused on its effects on dermal papilla cells expressing androgen receptor (AR). Accordingly, studies on the roles of DHT in keratinocytes, which undergo active proliferation and cell death during hair cycle progression, are lacking.

pmc-13617943.title: Comparative evaluation of remineralization agents in severe enamel hypomineralization using a porcine enamel model
pmc-13617943.creator: Aslı Aşık, Dilşah Çoğulu, Arzu Aykut Yetkiner, Nazan Ersin
pmc-13617943.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectivesTo comparatively evaluate the effects of fluoride varnish, casein phosphopeptide–amorphous calcium phosphate (CPP-ACP) varnish, and self-assembling peptide P11-4 on the microhardness and surface morphology of hypomineralized enamel using a porcine model simulating molar incisor hypomineralization (MIH).Materials and methodsEighteen hypomineralized primary canines and needle teeth (the erupted third incisors of newborn piglets) obtained from three stillborn Yorkshire piglets were included in this in vitro study.
